newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to tell G7 no need to worry on surplus -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to tell G7 no need to worry on surplus -- MOF.

text.p: Minister of Finance Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday that Japan would tell its partners in the Group of Seven (G7) nations that there is no need to worry about Japan's trade surplus mounting.

"I would like to tell them about the present state of our economy and its outlook and exchange views on this," he said, referring to the meeting of G7 finance ministers and central bankers to be held in Washington at the weekend.
"I would also like to tell them that there are hardly any worries that the surplus will mount, although I cannot say that there is no possibility at all," he said.
Mitsuzuka also said Japan would aim for stable economic management centring on domestic demand and that the G7 members would discuss what was meant by "stable currency rates".
Asked whether the G7 would confirm an agreement on currencies reached at its last meeting in Berlin in February, he said: "Yes, we will reaffirm the basics of the Berlin G7 agreement."
Mitsuzuka also said his ministry was arranging a bilateral meeting with U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin during his stay in Washington.
Mitsuzuka is due to arrive in Washington on Saturday and to leave on Tuesday.
